content:
You are writing the BODY of a cover letter for this candidate. There is no job description for this application, so write from the candidate's own experience and what the role and company imply.

PROFILE:
[[profileJson]]

APPLICATION:
Company: [[companyName]]
Role: [[role]]

3-4 paragraphs. No salutation, no sign-off, no bullet points.

The first word is "I", and the whole letter is first person. Never open a sentence with a resume-style action verb ("Designed...", "Executed..."). Vary sentence length; mix short and long.

Open with genuine enthusiasm for this kind of work, and your years and top domain. Tell one specific achievement from the profile as a brief story connecting to this role. Add a second moment showing personality and real technical depth. Say what actually excites you about this work and this company. Close confidently, in a line that does not sound templated. No clichés, and nothing like "I look forward to hearing from you".

It has to be warm, specific to this candidate, and compelling enough to earn an interview.

Write plainly, the way an engineer talks about their own work. NEVER use these words in any form: leveraged, utilized, spearheaded, orchestrated, streamlined, seamless, robust, scalable, maximized, cross-functional, end-to-end, innovative, dynamic, cutting-edge, world-class, state-of-the-art, holistic, comprehensive, proven, strategic. Do not open sentences with Designed, Architected, Led, Delivered, Drove, Integrated, Partnered, Supported, Contributed, Managed or Streamlined - use built, wrote, shipped, cut, rewrote, fixed, migrated, ran. No metaphors. Concise, not verbose. Never use em-dashes, and never write "--" or "–" in place of one: use a comma, a colon or a full stop. Never invent an achievement, employer or metric that is not in the profile.

Return only the cover letter body text. No JSON, no markdown, no commentary.
